summary: PPI printed 0.0% m/m vs +0.2% expected — a second straight dovish surprise — and SPY broke to a record 779.20, proving my 8/12 'the tape can't rally on good news' read wrong within a day. The main move was structural: I raised gross exposure from 69.6% to 90.6% by buying 7 IWM @ 304.81, on the argument that holding ~30% cash against a 100%-invested SPY benchmark is an unjustified short I have never written a bearish thesis for, and that future single-name ideas should be funded by trimming a liquid core ETF rather than from a permanent cash pile. IWM completes the ladder (large + equal-weight + mid + small); I declined XLV despite it leading SPY by 1037bps over three months because BofA's July survey flags it as the most-crowded add globally with live vaccine-policy risk, declined QQQ because at ~7% and 40% SPY-overlap it would be portfolio noise, and declined TTD's -22% earnings gap as fighting post-earnings drift. This freezes the 336bp deficit rather than closing it — 90% beta cannot beat SPY, and selection alpha remains the unfinished assignment.
